parsedVerdict.reasoning:
This unit has one file, src/auth/user.repository.ts, with one class, UserRepository. It extends BaseRepository<UserEntity, UserSerializer>, and all its members deal with the user record: creating it (store), looking it up (login, getUserForResetPassword) and turning it into the serializer (transform, transformMany). That is one concern, and the unit cannot split across files.

transform and transformMany override hooks that BaseRepository is typed for. They use class-transformer the same way the base class's generic parameters imply, so they work with the base abstraction rather than going around it.

There is a mild smell. login() holds authentication rules inside the persistence class: the password check through UserEntity.validatePassword, the check that the user is active, and the choice of ExceptionTitleList and StatusCodesList codes. store() also sets defaults: it uses INACTIVE when no status is given and generates the salt. This is business policy sitting in the repository. But each of these rules lives in exactly one place in the unit. The source shown proves no duplication, and the concerns are related rather than separate ones. JwtStrategy and JwtTwoFactorStrategy may repeat the active-status check, but their source was not provided, so duplication cannot be shown. On the evidence given, the unit meets the cohesion rule.
